preamble: The shift from the bilabial stop [p] to the velar stop [k] is known as velarization or revelation. It is a rare shift that typically occurs as part of a chain shift or through 'grave' consonant substitution, where two sounds at opposite ends of the mouth (lips and velum) are acoustically confused due to their similar low-frequency resonance.

examples.note: Northern Sami alone turned *p into k before a stop or sibilant; compare Lule Sami vuoppta, Inari vuopˈtâ.
Compare Lule Sami gippta, Skolt ǩiptt.
Compare Lule Sami sieppte, Inari septi.
Before a sibilant; compare Inari Sami lapse, South Sami lepsie.

sources: Campbell, L. (2013). Historical Linguistics: An Introduction (3rd ed.). Edinburgh University Press; MIT Press. https://lccn.loc.gov/2012038044
Sammallahti, P. (1998). The Saami Languages: An Introduction. Davvi Girji. https://lccn.loc.gov/00308815
